Hi Ellie — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can size the right Dedicated pathway (or confirm if Hosted/API can meet your needs).

Recap (from our notes):
- Primary workload: real-time summarization + user-facing chat for enterprise customers (support + insights).
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 300ms for single-turn generation in prod.
- Peak TPS estimate (you mentioned): ~85 TPS with significant bursts to ~200 TPS during reporting windows.
- Average request token mix: prompt ~420 tokens, completion ~120 tokens (tokenized) — sample will help.

Clarifying asks (can you confirm in reply):
1) Exact TPS baseline vs burst: is 85 TPS sustained or average? any hourly pattern?
2) Token distribution CSV you mentioned (sample for 1k requests) — please attach if available.
3) Are there plans to use multimodal inputs (images/attachments) in the next 6 months?
4) Security/placement preference: Dedicated (shared HW with isolation), Private VPC, or must be fully on-prem?

What we'll do next:
- Karthik will map these numbers to GPU-family options (A100 / H100 / L4 mix) and concurrent-connection strategies.
- We'll produce a short Dedicated vs Hosted decision matrix with cost and latency projections for your traffic shape.
- Draft a 4-week POC scope (pilot config + success criteria) after we get the sample token profile.

Attachments I will send: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.xlsx (baseline pricing tiers) and a POC scope template.

Thanks — one small ask: can you share the token profile CSV by Monday so we can run quick throughput estimates?

Hi Ellie / Vanessa — looked at the attached CSV. High-level technical readout and two recommended sizing options below. I'll keep the math simple here; we can share the notebook if you want the exact run.

Observations from token_profile (1k sample):
- Median prompt_tokens: 410, 95th percentile prompt: ~710
- Median completion: 110, 95th ~260
- Average total tokens/request ~520

Assumptions: target 95p latency <=300ms, batching allowed for non-100ms critical paths, KV cache hits expected ~10% for assisted prompts.

Option A — Low-latency priority (H100-heavy):
- GPU mix: H100 x4 nodes (NvLink enabled), each node can sustain ~35 TPS for your token profile with concurrency tuned to 48 streams.
- Fit: 85 steady TPS -> 3 nodes (safe buffer w/ autoscale to 4 for bursts). Bursts to 200 TPS -> autoscale to 6 nodes (fast-scaling policy).
- Pros: Meets 95p latency target comfortably; best single-token latency.
- Cons: Higher cost; H100 availability depends on region.

Option B — Cost-optimized (A100 + quantization):
- GPU mix: A100 x6 with quantized model (8-bit) and aggressive batching for throughput-oriented paths. Each node ~25 TPS sustained for this profile with concurrency ~96 streams.
- Fit: 85 steady -> 4 nodes; bursts -> scale to 8 nodes.
- Pros: Much better cost per token; simpler capacity planning in most clouds.
- Cons: Slightly wider latency tail; may require tuning for prompt-critical flows.

Operational notes:
- We recommend a hybrid routing policy: critical routes (support chat) go to H100-backed pool; background summarization to A100 pool with autoscaling and cache-enabled.
- POC success criteria: 95p latency <=300ms on critical route, <1% error rate, sustained 85 TPS for 2 hours in staging with scaling events captured.

Next ask from us: can Skylab scope a short load-window (2-hour sustained 85 TPS + a 15-minute 200 TPS burst) in stage where we can run the pilot? Also confirm any network egress constraints.

- Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer — Redwood Inference
